product_overview: HiPat QA Test is designed to verify the functionality and reliability of a personality-governed AI assistant platform that dynamically routes user queries to specialized roles and skills, ensuring high-quality, auditable, and secure interactive experiences.
core_goals: Confirm the correct personality profile governs all AI responses and routing.
Ensure new roles and skills can be added and routed dynamically without code changes.
Detect defects in routing, prompts, role-level security (RLS), logs, and administrative UI CRUD operations.
Validate that all AI responses include personality injection with a consistent tone and style.
Verify that skill outputs conform to strict JSON schemas and error structures.
Confirm audit logging of all admin changes and user interactions without leaking PII.
Ensure all security policies and row-level security prevent unauthorized data access.
Achieve high system performance with 50th percentile response times under 2 seconds without external API calls.
Establish robust fallback behaviors for disabled or failing external APIs.
Validate end-to-end user flows from trigger detection to response generation with appropriate logs and audit data.
key_features: Personality layer injected in every AI response enforcing a first-person, spartan tone.
Multi-agent routing system with priorities that select relevant roles and skills based on user triggers.
Comprehensive skill set including macro_lookup, food_search, barcode_parse, workout_parse, rag_lookup, and extensible skill additions.
Administrative UI for managing personal profiles, roles, skills, prompts, routes, agent-skill links, testbench, and auditing.
Detailed logging and telemetry including routing paths, skills fired, model identifiers, token usage, and cost tracking.
Role-based access control and row-level security ensuring proper data access and modification permissions.
Real-time detection and routing based on user input triggers with fallback skill behavior.
Contract schema enforcement for each skill's JSON output and structured error handling.
Voice and chat interface integration with persistent chat history and preferences.
Content guardrails preventing unsolicited plant-based suggestions and handling medical topics appropriately.
user_flow_summary: User submits a message via chat interface.
System injects the active Personality into the response context to govern tone and style.
Router analyzes the message triggers and selects one or more relevant skills based on predefined priorities.
Selected skills process the input and return structured JSON output conforming to contract schemas.
Personality composes the final response incorporating skill data, maintaining tone consistency.
Response and metadata including personality ID, agent ID, routes hit, skills fired, model, tokens, and cost are logged for audit and telemetry.
Admin UI CRUD operations allow managing personalities, skills, roles, prompts, routes, and agent-skill relationships dynamically.
Audit logs record all changes made via admin panel for traceability and monitoring.
Security mechanisms enforce role-based access and prevent unauthorized data access or modifications.
System handles cases with no-route matches by falling back to AMA role responses.
Extended user input with compound intents are handled deterministically with logged rationale.
validation_criteria: Table presence and consistency checks for all required Supabase tables.
Exactly one active personality profile must exist and be enforced as exclusive.
AMA role and seed skills must exist and be functional.
Routing triggers must correctly select appropriate skills and produce matching logs.
Skill outputs must strictly adhere to JSON schema requirements or deliver structured errors.
Administrative changes must persist immediately and be logged in audit events.
All messages must include detailed metadata for telemetry including tokens and costs.
Unauthorized access attempts must be denied per RLS policies.
No PII should appear in any logs or telemetry data.
Performance benchmark of median response under 2 seconds when external API calls are disabled.
Fallback stubs or structured errors must be returned when external APIs fail or are unreachable.
Content guardrails must prevent unauthorized plant-based suggestions except when explicitly requested.
Pass/fail criteria include achieving 95%+ success rate in routing, personality injection, security, and schema validation.
Failures must be reported with detailed input, observed vs expected outcomes, relevant logs, and minimal repro steps.
